chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Is'haq ibn Muhammad al-Nakha'i, from Abu Hashim Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) when permission was sought for a man from the people of Yemen to see him. So there entered a man who was stout, tall, and large. He greeted him (peace be upon him) with the acknowledgment of wilayah, and he (peace be upon him) responded with acceptance and commanded him to sit. He sat down adjacent to me. I said to myself: 'If only I knew who this person is.'

Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: 'This one is from the descendants of the Bedouin woman, the owner of the pebble in which my forefathers (peace be upon them) had imprinted their signet rings and it was engraved. He has come with it, intending that I should imprint (my seal) in it.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Give it here!' So he brought out a pebble, and on one side of it was a smooth surface. Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) took it, then brought out his signet ring and imprinted it therein, and it was engraved. It was as though I could see the engraving of his seal ring at that very moment: 'al-Hasan ibn Ali.' Then I said to the Yemeni: 'Had you ever seen him before this?'
He said: 'No, by Allah; and I have for a long time been eager to see him, until just now a youth came to me whom I cannot see (anymore), and he said to me: Arise and enter. So I entered.'

Then the Yemeni stood up and was saying: 'May Allah's mercy and His blessings be upon you, O People of the Household — a progeny, one from another. I testify by Allah that your right is obligatory, just as the obligation of the right of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and the Imams after him — may Allah's salawat be upon them all.' Then he departed, and I did not see him after that.

Is'haq said: Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari said: I asked him about his name, and he said: 'My name is Mihja' ibn al-Salt ibn Uqba ibn Sim'an ibn Ghanim, son of Umm Ghanim; and she was the Yemenite Bedouin woman, the owner of the pebble in which the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and his descendants had imprinted, up to the time of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.الأعرابية: The Bedouin woman — the original owner of the pebble, from whom this man is descended; refers to a woman from Yemen who had this stone blessed by Imam Ali (AS)
key_terms.الحصاة: The pebble — a miraculous stone kept as a family heirloom across generations, bearing the seal impressions of the Imams
key_terms.الخاتم / خواتيم: Signet ring(s) — used to imprint official seals; the Imams' seals on the pebble serve as authentication of their Imamate
key_terms.السبط: Descendants (sibt) — referring to the Imams descended from the Prophet through Fatima al-Zahra
key_terms.الولاية: Wilayah — the authority and guardianship of the Imam; greeting 'with wilayah' means acknowledging the Imam's divinely appointed authority
key_terms.ذرية بعضها من بعض: A progeny, one from another (Quran 3:34) — cited to affirm the hereditary nature of the Imamate

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the pebble stamped by the Imams in the time of Imam al-Askari?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a remarkable encounter at the court of Imam Hasan al-Askari (AS), the eleventh Imam, in which a Yemeni visitor presents a sacred pebble that had been miraculously engraved with the seal rings of all previous Imams. The Imam reads the man's unspoken thought — a demonstration of his supernatural knowledge — then stamps the pebble, adding his own seal to the lineage of Imamate seals. The Yemeni's concluding testimony, citing the Quranic phrase 'a progeny, one from another' (3:34), affirms the continuous, divinely sanctioned authority of the Imams as a hereditary spiritual line.
